title: Roy Williams: From OU's Superman to Five Straight Pro Bowls
question: How many Pro Bowls did former Oklahoma safety Roy Williams make in the NFL?
answer: Five. Roy Williams (OU 1999-2001), the No. 8 overall pick of the Dallas Cowboys in 2002, made five consecutive Pro Bowls for the 2003 through 2007 seasons and was a first-team All-Pro in 2003.
summary: Ex-Sooner safety Roy Williams went No. 8 overall in 2002 and made five straight Pro Bowls with Dallas. His OU awards, NFL career and Hall of Fame honors.
body: Roy Williams (OU 1999-2001) arrived in Norman from Union City, California, and left as one of the most decorated defenders in Sooner history. He started on the 2000 national title team, and in 2001 he became the first player ever to win the Bronko Nagurski Trophy and the Jim Thorpe Award in the same season, along with Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year and unanimous All-America honors.

Fans remember him best for the 2001 Red River game, when he soared over the line to hit Texas quarterback Chris Simms, jarring the ball loose for Teddy Lehman's clinching touchdown in a 14-3 win. That play gave him his famous nickname, Superman.

Leaving a year early, Williams went eighth overall to the Dallas Cowboys in 2002 and made an instant impact. As a rookie he intercepted five passes and returned two for touchdowns, tying a Cowboys single-season record, and finished as runner-up for Defensive Rookie of the Year. He then made five straight Pro Bowls, for the 2003 through 2007 seasons, and was a first-team All-Pro in 2003.
After seven seasons in Dallas, he finished his career with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2009 and 2010, retiring with 20 career interceptions.

The honors kept coming afterward. Williams entered the Cotton Bowl Hall of Fame and, in 2022, the College Football Hall of Fame as the 23rd Sooner player enshrined. OU's Roy Williams Strength and Speed Complex carries his name, and his Roy Williams Safety Net Foundation supports low-income single mothers.
